forbidden: Do not port a rule you cannot make fail on purpose.
Do not promote any ported rule past candidate.
Do not port all 148 in one pass.
objective: The other surface produced 148 atomic rules with 12 tests. They are a source of candidates, not a rule base. Bring them in under the lifecycle so the untested ones are visibly untested rather than quietly in force.
reconciliation_note: Written before the Rules Engineering baseline was promoted to OPERATIVE. The packet says port the v0.2 rules as candidates, which is wrong against an operative set: importing an operative rule as a candidate silently downgrades it. Rewrite the objective against the operative baseline before running. Note also the near certain rule id collision: this package uses TASK-01, ASSET-01 and similar generic ids, and a 148 rule set with entity rules for the same five entities almost certainly uses some of them too.
report: How many ported, how many refused and why.
The health findings after each batch.
The rule count and the case count, which should stay at parity.
steps: Take them in batches of ten, not all at once.

For each, write the predicate against the shared library in predicates.py rather than inline. Two rules expressing one condition in two slightly different ways is how a rule base starts contradicting itself.
Every ported rule enters as a candidate. Candidates refuse nothing, so a wrong port costs nothing until someone promotes it.
A rule you cannot write a refusal case for does not get ported. Record it in a list of rules that could not be made falsifiable and move on.
Check the register health output after each batch, particularly the duplicate and overlapping findings.
title: Port the v0.2 rules into the register as candidates
